title: Risk of Performance Decrements and Adverse Health Outcomes Resulting from Sleep Loss, Circadian Desynchronization, and Work Overload
used_for: Sleep and circadian context for evidence cards and explanations. Does not establish ASTRA's deviation thresholds, explain an individual's HRV, or validate scenario benefits.
summary: NASA describes sleep loss, disrupted circadian timing, and environmental interference with sleep as concerns for crew performance. ASTRA uses this research context to explain why a sleep trend may merit review.

title: Human System Risks
used_for: Research risk taxonomy and contextual links for the science page and review findings. The catalog does not supply ASTRA telemetry or validate its unitless prototype signal categories.
summary: NASA's catalog includes sleep, cardiovascular, muscle, bone, radiation, and cabin carbon dioxide risks. These categories frame ASTRA's research references; fictional daily readings and fixture-specific rules remain separate.

title: Risks of Human Spaceflight
used_for: Mission context and limitations for the science page and illustrative sleep/exercise planning comparisons. No NASA effect size or clinical prediction is implemented from this page.
summary: NASA organizes human-spaceflight risks around radiation, isolation and confinement, distance from Earth, gravity changes, and hostile or closed environments. Its overview includes sleep and fitness research, providing context rather than a personalized prediction model.
